market_summary: Post-market wrap for Friday 27 November 2026 (as of 19:28 IST; next Indian cash session is Monday 30 November). The Nifty 50 fell 277.30 points (-1.07%) to 25,607.20 and the Sensex fell 989.33 points (-1.17%) to 83,339.26, ending a two-day advance and snapping the four-week winning streak; both benchmarks lost about 0.7% for the week. Twelve of 16 major sectors declined, according to Reuters. IT was the weakest major sector (Nifty IT -1.88%), with auto (-1.48%), realty (-1.43%) and financials also under pressure; metals (+1.40%) and media (+0.53%) were relative gainers. Brent rose above $97/bbl amid Middle East supply concerns, while the rupee weakened 0.6% to ₹92.99 per US dollar. Provisional 27 November cash-market flows showed FII/FPI net buying of ₹1,634.33 crore and DII net selling of ₹556.42 crore; these are provisional third-party reproductions of NSE data, not final settled figures. Global equities rebounded across Asia and Europe after the US Thanksgiving holiday, and US index futures were higher, but this divergence did not prevent Indian equities from falling. A verified NSE filing confirmed Alivus Life Sciences completed the acquisition of a 76% stake in IQGEN-X; Eros International Media disclosed its CEO/Executive Director's resignation effective 30 November. The public portfolio data file lists M&M and SBIN as watchlist candidates, not actual holdings; no holdings ledger was accessible, so portfolio-specific exposure could not be verified. Facts and interpretation are separated below. No guaranteed calls or financial advice.

global_cues.title: Global equities rebounded after Thanksgiving, led by Asia and technology shares
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported Japan's Nikkei +2.1%, China's blue-chip market +4.2%, European shares +0.8%, Nasdaq futures +2.1% and S&P 500 futures +1.5% on Friday. Chinese shares rose after Beijing announced further capital-market support. US cash equities had been closed for Thanksgiving on Thursday and were scheduled for a shortened Friday session. Interpretation: the global risk rebound was a positive external cue, but Indian benchmarks sold off despite it; thin holiday liquidity and the durability of the AI-led recovery remain risks.

global_cues.title: Oil climbed above $97 as Middle East supply concerns intensified
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported Brent above $96.50/bbl amid supply concerns and regional tensions. Separately, the Indian market close report put Brent at about $97.22/bbl. Interpretation: higher crude is a macro headwind for an oil-importing economy and can pressure the rupee, inflation expectations and fuel-sensitive sectors; the quoted levels are reported market observations, not live ticks.

global_cues.title: China policy support and the AI trade helped lift regional risk appetite
global_cues.detail: The Associated Press reported Shanghai's Composite +3.7%, South Korea's Kospi +4.3%, Japan's Nikkei +2.1% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng +2.1% on Friday. AP attributed the Chinese-market strength partly to authorities signalling stronger stock-market support. Interpretation: these moves support regional sentiment, but do not by themselves establish a direct earnings catalyst for Indian listed companies.

intraday.headline: CEO and Executive Director Pradeep Kumar Dwivedi resigns, effective 30 November
intraday.what_changed: Verified fact: the company's Regulation 30 filing states that Pradeep Kumar Dwivedi tendered his resignation as CEO, Key Managerial Personnel and Executive Director on 27 November for personal reasons. The resignation takes effect at the close of business on 30 November 2026. The filing says he cited no other material reason.
intraday.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the departure creates a near-term leadership transition at the company. Investors may look for a successor announcement and clarity on continuity of operating responsibilities; the filing itself does not quantify any financial impact.
intraday.risk: The stated reason is personal and no successor details are included in the filing. The impact depends on transition arrangements and subsequent company disclosures; avoid inferring operational disruption from the resignation alone.
intraday.source: Eros International Media Limited, Regulation 30 filing to NSE/BSE, 27 Nov 2026; listed by NSE at 18:51:34 IST

swing.headline: Completes acquisition of remaining 10.99% in IQGEN-X; total stake reaches 76%
swing.what_changed: Verified fact: Alivus's Regulation 30 filing says it completed the purchase of the remaining 1,24,493 equity shares, representing 10.99% of IQGEN-X Pharma Private Limited's issued and paid-up equity capital. The company states that closing under the share purchase agreement is complete and that its total stake in IQGEN-X is now 76%.
swing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: completion removes the execution uncertainty around this tranche and gives Alivus a controlling 76% interest in IQGEN-X. The filing does not disclose purchase consideration, IQGEN-X's financial contribution or expected synergies, so the earnings impact cannot yet be assessed.
swing.risk: Acquisition economics, integration requirements, funding impact and IQGEN-X's financial performance were not quantified in this filing. Control does not guarantee accretion or successful integration.
swing.source: Alivus Life Sciences Limited, Regulation 30 filing to NSE/BSE, 27 Nov 2026; listed by NSE at 18:51:42 IST
